categories.title: Simplicity & scope
categories.description: Prefer the smallest correct solution for current requirements; avoid legacy drag and speculative work.

categories.title: Architecture
categories.description: How code is structured and how durable design choices are made — modularity, separation of concerns, and long-lived decisions.

categories.title: Dependencies
categories.description: How to choose libraries: prefer what the project already has, then solid maintained packages, before writing your own.

entries.title: No backward compatibility
entries.picker: Drop legacy contracts freely; current correctness beats old callers.

entries.title: Simplest that meets current requirements
entries.picker: No speculative complexity — fully meet what is required now, nothing more.
inject: Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirements. Do not add speculative complexity for needs that are not required yet.

entries.title: Prefer maintained libraries
entries.picker: Use established, well-maintained libraries instead of hand-rolled equivalents.
inject: Prefer established, well-maintained libraries over custom implementations.

entries.title: Lean on dependencies already in the project
entries.picker: Use what the project already depends on before writing new code or adding packages; check docs and types first.
inject: Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a capability without checking its documentation and types.

entries.title: Durable architectural decisions
entries.picker: When a real architectural choice is required, make one meant to last — no planned throwaways.
inject: When a real architectural decision is required, choose a design meant to last. Do not accept a stopgap intended only to work for now and be replaced later.

entries.title: Modular components and separated concerns
entries.picker: Keep components modular; keep concerns clearly separated.
inject: Keep components modular and concerns clearly separated.
